title: The false sunset
hookLine: a vow with a sunset deadline, and a sun that seems to set too early

lines: DRONA HIDES HIM AT THE BACK.
cards: The news of Arjuna's vow reaches Jayadratha in the night, and he wants to leave the war and go home. Drona talks him out of it. Stay, he says, and I'll protect you.
So in the morning Drona builds his army into layer after layer, and places Jayadratha far at the back, behind all of it. Arjuna has one day to cut through to a man hidden behind a whole army.
Every hour the sun climbs, then starts to fall.

teach.b: Arjuna and Krishna drive into the ranks, and the fighting goes on hour after hour. At one point the horses are worn out.

In Ganguli's telling, Arjuna stands guard with his bow while Krishna unyokes them and lets them drink and rest, right there in the middle of the battle. But the sun keeps falling, and Jayadratha is still out of reach.

Darkness spreads over the field, and the text says Krishna brought it about by his own power. The Kauravas see what looks like sunset, and they cheer. Jayadratha, safe at last, raises his head to look at the sky.
The sun is still up. And Arjuna's arrow takes Jayadratha's head, carrying it into the lap of his father, who had cursed anyone who made it fall to the ground.

When the old king rises from his evening prayer, the head drops, and the curse falls on him. The epic doesn't hide the trick, and readers still argue about it. But here's what Hindus who love Krishna hear in this day.
Arjuna had staked his life on a vow too big for one man.
In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells him: declare it boldly, my devotee never perishes.
That's bhakti, loving trust in God, and this is its heart: the one who leans on Krishna isn't left alone when his own strength runs out.
Many Hindus pray just this way when a day is slipping from them: I've done what I can; the rest is yours.

how: The day of Jayadratha's death is told in the Drona Parva, and retellings return to the false sunset and Krishna's part in it.

o: the false sunset that Krishna brings down over the whole field
the commander who hides Jayadratha at the very back of his army
the old king whose curse falls back on his own head instead

games.q: the race against the sun — tap the pairs.

s: in Hindu devotion, Krishna leaves his devotee to manage alone once things get hard
the Gita promises the opposite: my devotee never perishes. bhakti trusts God to stand with you.
Krishna rested and watered the horses in the middle of the battle
Arjuna stood guard while Krishna unyoked them.
the sun had truly set when Arjuna struck
the text says Krishna brought the darkness; the sun was still up.

games.q: Arjuna has staked his life on a vow, and the sun is falling. by the bhakti in today's story, what does he lean on?
o: his own strength alone, harder and harder.
Krishna at the reins, who stands with him.
luck: a vow is a coin toss.
games.why: Arjuna fights with everything he has, and Krishna carries what he can't. Hindus hear the Gita's promise in it: my devotee never perishes.

practice: Many Hindus keep a short prayer for days like this: a name of Krishna, or simply, Krishna, I leave it with you. Think of something you're racing against today. Breathing in, feel how tightly it holds you.
Breathing out, say the name or the prayer, and let your hands loosen, the way Krishna watered the horses mid-battle; the race will still be there.
If you don't pray, just rest in the out-breath and let what you can't control sit beside you.

wordCard.voice: Drona. Today he hides Jayadratha behind his whole army, and the hiding place doesn't hold.

orig.note: the king of Sindhu who held the gap, and the target of Arjuna's vow.

carryVoice: Your line: bhakti: my devotee never perishes. Arjuna's vow was too big for one man, and he wasn't alone. Day eight hundred thirty-four, done.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Jayadratha-vadha Parva), Drona's protection of Jayadratha, the horses watered, the darkness and Jayadratha's death
Bhagavad Gita 9.31 (Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva), Krishna: declare boldly that my devotee never perishes
